runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current official council pages, explicit CIL/S106 role separation, monitoring-period controls and prevention of infrastructure-policy evidence being misused as parcel liability, viability or delivery proof.

sources.label: LBBD Developer contributions overview
sources.fact: CIL helps fund infrastructure needed to accommodate growth; Section 106 can secure financial/non-financial contributions including affordable housing or mitigation works.

sources.label: LBBD borough CIL
sources.fact: Borough CIL came into effect 3 April 2015; council page lists an Annual CIL Rate Summary 2026. Actual liability remains development-specific.

sources.label: LBBD CIL guidance
sources.fact: New-build floorspace of 100 square metres or more or development creating a residential dwelling may be CIL-liable; liability/relief/commencement follow formal process.

sources.label: LBBD Mayor of London CIL guidance
sources.fact: Council page distinguishes MCIL1 and MCIL2 and states MCIL2 applies to permissions granted on or after 1 April 2019.

sources.label: LBBD Section 106 guidance
sources.fact: Council directs users to the Planning Obligations SPD for its approach to securing Section 106 planning obligations.

sources.label: LBBD Section 106 monitoring
sources.fact: Council publishes historic Section 106 receipts/agreements information; historic receipts cannot establish a future parcel-specific obligation.

sources.label: LBBD Infrastructure Funding Statements
sources.fact: Council is required to publish an annual Infrastructure Funding Statement for CIL and Section 106; page currently lists statements through 1 April 2023-31 March 2024.

sources.label: LBBD Supplementary Planning Documents
sources.fact: Planning Obligations SPD was adopted 18 September 2024; it is a material consideration and provides up-to-date guidance for S106 alongside CIL.

sources.label: LBBD Inclusive Growth - Infrastructure and Transport
sources.fact: Infrastructure Delivery Plan assesses current infrastructure provision and future requirements; Transport Strategy supports Local Plan housing, air-quality and travel-behaviour objectives.

sources.label: LBBD Roads and transport plan
sources.fact: LIP3 sets a borough transport-improvement strategy to 2041; it was agreed in January 2019 and approved by the Mayor in April 2019.

sources.label: LBBD Planning
sources.fact: Be First provides statutory planning services on behalf of the council; planning-policy and application decisions remain formal processes rather than inferred from growth evidence.

sources.label: LBBD plans for homes summary
sources.fact: Council states a need to build more homes and prioritise council-built homes for local people; strategic ambition is not evidence of permission, viability or delivery on a specific parcel.

examples.result: LBBD49/XJ Former Ford Stamping Plant remains an official current growth candidate, but CIL/S106 framework evidence does not prove site delivery or parcel-specific liability; no promotion.
LBBD72/ZZ GSR and Gill Sites remains an official current candidate; permission status plus contribution policy still does not establish exact parcel relation or future delivery; no promotion.
LBBD64/XE Ibscott Close Estate remains not-permissioned in the current candidate evidence; infrastructure-policy pages cannot override that status; no promotion.
LBBD91/DI 53-135 Roxwell Road remains a current official candidate; CIL/S106/transport strategy is contextual only until exact geometry and site-specific planning evidence are bound.
CIL threshold/process revalidated: potential liability is development-specific and cannot be calculated from parcel area or growth score alone.
S106 and CIL roles revalidated as distinct mechanisms; neither historic receipts nor generic SPD guidance proves a future obligation for an unverified parcel.
Latest IFS publicly listed on the council page covers 1 April 2023-31 March 2024; reporting period is retained and not silently treated as 2026 transaction evidence.
LIP3/Infrastructure Delivery Plan are strategic delivery evidence; transport or infrastructure ambition is not converted into parcel-level completion probability without project/site binding.
